ss_open.source: E. Sandier and S. Serfaty, From the Ginzburg-Landau Model to Vortex Lattice Problems, arXiv:1011.4617v2 (second version, January 2012)
ss_open.text: We introduce a Coulombian renormalized energy W which is a logarithmic type of interaction between points in the plane, computed by a renormalization. We prove various of its properties, such as the existence of minimizers, and show in particular, using results from number theory, that among lattice configurations the triangular lattice is the unique minimizer. Its minimization in general remains open.

ss_conj.text: Theorem 2. Let L = {Lambda | Lambda is a lattice and j_Lambda in A_m}. Then the minimum of Lambda -> W(Lambda) over L is achieved uniquely, modulo rotation, by the triangular lattice Lambda_m = sqrt(4 pi / (m sqrt 3)) ((1,0)Z + (1/2, sqrt3/2)Z). ... Conjecture 1. The lattice Lambda_m being defined as in Theorem 2, we have W(Lambda_m) = min_{A_m} W.

ss_prop49.text: Proposition 4.9. Assume U in R^2 is open and (j, nu) are such that nu = 2 pi sum_{p in Lambda} delta_p for some finite subset Lambda of U-hat and curl j = nu - m, div j = 0 in U-hat, where m in L^infinity(U-hat). Then there exists a measure g supported on U-hat and such that - g >= -C(||m||_infinity^2 + 1) on U-hat, where C is a universal constant. - For any function chi compactly supported in U we have (4.12) | W(j, chi) - int chi dg | <= C n (log n + ||m||_infinity) ||grad chi||_infinity, where n = #{p in Lambda | B(p, C) intersect Supp(grad chi) is nonempty} and C is universal.

ss_prop31.text: Proposition 3.1. Assume Lambda = Z u + Z v and j are as above. Then, letting {U_R} be any family satisfying (1.4), defining W_U(j) as in (1.8) we have (3.1) W_U(j) = lim_{eta->0} (1/2 pi) ((1/2) int_{T_Lambda minus B(0,eta)} |j|^2 + pi log eta). Moreover, letting H_Lambda be the unique solution (with mean zero) on T_Lambda to (3.2) -Delta H_Lambda = 2 pi delta_0 - 1, and denoting (3.3) j_Lambda = -grad^perp H_Lambda we have that j - j_Lambda is a constant and W_U(j) >= W_U(j_Lambda) with equality if and only if j = j_Lambda.

bs_thm15.source: L. Betermin and E. Sandier, Renormalized Energy and Asymptotic Expansion of Optimal Logarithmic Energy on the Sphere, arXiv:1404.4485v5 (April 2018)
bs_thm15.text: Theorem 1.5. There exists C != 0 independent of n such that, as n -> +infinity, E_log(n) = (1/2 - log 2) n^2 - (n/2) log n + C n + o(n), C = (1/pi) min_{A_1} W + (log pi)/2 + log 2. Moreover C <= C_BHS where C_BHS is given in (1.5), and equality holds iff min_{A_1} W is achieved for the triangular lattice of density one.

bhs_conj4.source: J. S. Brauchart, D. P. Hardin, E. B. Saff, The next-order term for optimal Riesz and logarithmic energy asymptotics on the sphere, arXiv:1202.4037v1
bhs_conj4.text: Conjecture 4. For d = 2, 4, 8, and 24, (30) E_log(S^d; N) = V_log(S^d) N^2 - (1/d) N log N + C_{log,d} N + o(N), as N -> infinity, where the constant of the N-term is given by (31) C_{log,d} = (1/d) log(H_d(S^d)/|Lambda_d|) + zeta'_{Lambda_d}(0). For the case d = 2, (31) reduces to C_{log,2} = 2 log 2 + (1/2) log (2/3) + 3 log (sqrt(pi)/Gamma(1/3)) = -0.05560530494339251850... < 0.
